item.title: Flying Fijians must stay disciplined and connected for full 80 minutes - Seruvakula
item.description: The FIJI Water Flying Fijians will need to be disciplined on both sides of the ball, and stay connected for the full 80 minutes as they prepare to take on Canada tonight. Those were the words of Interim Coach Senirusi Seruvakula from Japan, saying that they will never underestimate Canada as they are a very good side.
item.content:encoded:
The FIJI Water Flying Fijians will need to be disciplined on both sides of the ball, and stay connected for the full 80 minutes as they prepare to take on Canada tonight.

Those were the words of Interim Coach Senirusi Seruvakula from Japan, saying that they will never underestimate Canada as they are a very good side.

Seruvakula says Canada has an advantage over them as they played Japan last weekend.

He says they currently have no injuries in the squad and are looking forward to tonight's game.

Skipper Tevita Ikanivere says they have had a great preparation for the past two weeks, and the boys are excited to play Canada tonight.

Ikanivere also mentioned that they have four debutants for this game in No. 8 Isoa Tuwai, Penaia Cakobau, Inoke Ravuiwasa and Terio Tamani.

The Flying Fijians are the current defending Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup champions.

Fiji will take on Canada at 7 tonight in Osaka.

Meanwhile, Japan will meet the USA at 10pm.

item.title: Family support helps Savusavu woman fulfil father’s dream of becoming a teacher
item.description: For Shinal Devi of Buca, Savusavu, becoming a teacher was more than a career choice - it was a dream her father had for her from a very young age, and one she has now fulfilled. Devi has graduated from the University of the South Pacific with a Bachelor of Education (Primary).
item.content:encoded:
For Shinal Devi of Buca, Savusavu, becoming a teacher was more than a career choice - it was a dream her father had for her from a very young age, and one she has now fulfilled.

Devi has graduated from the University of the South Pacific with a Bachelor of Education (Primary).

She says her decision to become a teacher was largely influenced by her father.

Devi dedicates her achievement to her husband, parents, sisters and two children, who supported her throughout her studies.

She says the journey was not easy as she had to balance her studies with family commitments and responsibilities.

She says her Year 5 daughter was one of her biggest supporters and would encourage her whenever she was feeling down.

She adds that despite her young age, her daughter understood what she was going through and would often tell her that she wanted to see her graduate and wear her graduation cap.

Devi says her husband was unable to attend the graduation in person but watched the ceremony live from home.

She also thanked her parents and sister for the support they provided throughout her journey.

Devi is encouraging students to remain committed to their studies, saying education plays an important role in people's lives, particularly in today’s world.

She hopes students will one day experience their own graduation moment, whether they are pursuing a degree, master’s degree, diploma or certificate.

item.title: Three-month-old Marina given new hope after heart treatment in Fiji
item.description: Marina was discharged from the Sri Sathya Sai Sanjeevani Children’s Hospital, after receiving treatment for a heart condition that was discovered shortly after birth. She was among three children discharged from the Sri Sathya Sai Sanjeevani Children’s Hospital after receiving treatment for heart conditions.
item.content:encoded:
Marina was discharged from the Sri Sathya Sai Sanjeevani Children’s Hospital, after receiving treatment for a heart condition that was discovered shortly after birth.

She was among three children discharged from the Sri Sathya Sai Sanjeevani Children’s Hospital after receiving treatment for heart conditions.

Tirii says the family did not know Marina had a heart condition at birth, but doctors detected a heart murmur after she became sick during her first week of life.

Further tests later confirmed that Marina had a large ventricular septal defect, or VSD, which is a hole in the heart.

Tirii says finding out that her first child had a heart condition was difficult and unexpected.

Marina continued to receive medical check-ups in the Solomon Islands before arrangements were made for the mother and daughter to travel to Fiji for treatment.

Tirii says travelling away from home with her three-month-old baby was not easy, but she is grateful her daughter was able to receive the care she needed.

She has thanked the Solomon Islands Government for supporting their journey to Fiji, as well as the surgeons, donors and medical teams involved in Marina’s care.

After the uncertainty surrounding her daughter’s condition and the journey away from home for treatment, Tirii is now grateful to be leaving hospital with Marina and looking forward to taking her home.

item.title: 9/11 changed the face of global security - Tikoduadua
item.description: The events of September 11th changed the face of global security, and the world was never the same after 2001. Minister for Defence Pio Tikoduadua highlighted this while speaking to the media after the 25th anniversary commemoration of 9/11 at the US Embassy.
item.content:encoded:
The events of September 11th changed the face of global security, and the world was never the same after 2001.

Minister for Defence Pio Tikoduadua highlighted this while speaking to the media after the 25th anniversary commemoration of 9/11 at the US Embassy.

Tikoduadua says the United States remains a strong partner of Fiji, with the two countries standing together during times of war and peace.

He says the partnership is built on shared democratic values and principles.

Tikoduadua says while it is important to remember the past, the focus should be on making the future better for the next generation.

The Defence Minister says the events of September 11th will always affect people in different ways.

Insert: Tikoduadua moving forward Sep 11

The commemoration at the US Embassy was attended by government officials, members of the armed forces, the diplomatic corps and other guests.
